acts.title: Text A · Four things that were entered for one prize
text: The James Dyson Award was created in 2007 to push engineering students towards ideas that are actually built. Four entries are described below, and none of them is a concept drawing.

The first is a printer that has been designed to take up almost no space. It is placed on top of a stack of paper and moves slowly downwards as it works; the paper disappears underneath and is delivered on top.

The second is worn inside the mouth. It protects the teeth of Gaelic football players, and while it is being worn the player is monitored for injury. If somebody is moving more slowly than usual, that is measured and sent wirelessly to a computer, and the player is taken off to be treated.
The third can be attached to almost anything and used to generate electricity from wind. The energy that has been generated is then used to recharge a phone.
The fourth is fixed to a window. Outside noise is reduced, and — the remarkable part — the wearer chooses which sounds are removed.

items.q: What do the four entries have in common?
o: They are working devices, not concept drawings
They were all built in Ireland

items.q: What does the second device do besides protecting teeth?
o: It monitors the player for injury and reports wirelessly

acts.title: Text B · The one that came from a beetle
text: The problem of drought-affected farmers may have been partly solved by an earlier winner of the same award.

Edward Linacre had been inspired by the worst Australian drought in a century. His device, Airdrop, collects water out of the air: moisture is drawn from the atmosphere, cooled underground, and delivered directly to the roots of the crop.

The idea was given to him by an insect. The Namib beetle survives in one of the driest places on earth by collecting tiny amounts of moisture on its own back, and Linacre simply asked what would happen if that were done at scale.

Up until now the system has been developed in his mother’s back garden. Linacre has since been asked to develop it by the Chinese government and by companies in the Middle East. He has not agreed yet. In the future it will be taken up to an industrial level; for the moment he would rather keep working on it himself.

items.s: Airdrop collects water from the air rather than from the ground.
The idea came from an insect that collects moisture on its back.
The system was developed in a university laboratory.
Linacre has been approached by the Chinese government.
He has already agreed to hand the project over.

items.q: What do all six sentences have in common?
o: They are passive: a form of be plus a past participle
They all name who did it

items.q: “While it is being worn…” — which tense is this?
“may have been partly solved” — what is happening here?
o: A modal plus the perfect passive

items.q: Why does the writer use the passive so heavily here?
o: The device matters and the person does not

acts.title: The passive, in every form you will need
rule: The passive moves the important thing to the front of the sentence. It is not a way of sounding academic — it is what you use when the thing done matters more than the person who did it, which is most of the time in a description of how something works.
points: A form of be + past participle. Only be changes; the participle stays still.
Include it only when the agent adds information. Most passive sentences do not need one.
modal + be + past participle. It can be attached to anything.
modal + have been + past participle. It may have been solved.
A verb like give has two, so either can go first: The idea was given to him. He was given the idea.
eg: It is placed on a stack of paper.
Present simple passive.
While it is being worn, the player is monitored.
Present continuous passive.
The system has been developed in a back garden.
Present perfect passive.
The idea was given to him by a beetle.
Past simple passive, with a by-agent that earns its place.
He was given the idea by a beetle.
The same sentence, other object first.
Linacre had been inspired by a drought.
Past perfect passive.
It will be taken up to an industrial level.
Future passive.
It can be attached to almost anything.
Modal + be + participle.
The problem may have been solved.
Modal + have been + participle.
Two out of three players had been injured.
Past perfect passive, no agent — nobody injured them deliberately.
acts.careful: “It was stole” and “It can seen” are the two commonest errors. The passive needs the past participle, and after a modal it needs be in front of it.

acts.title: Active into passive, in four moves
steps: A team in Austria designed the device in 2013.
1 · Move the OBJECT to the front. It becomes the new subject.
2 · Put BE into the tense of the original verb: designed → was.
3 · Add the PAST PARTICIPLE of the main verb.
4 · Add by + agent only if it matters. Here it does not, so leave it out.

lines: The printer [is placed|places|is placing] on top of a stack of paper.
While the guard [is being worn|is wearing|has worn], the player is monitored.
The system [has been developed|has developed|is developing] in a back garden.
The device [can be attached|can attach|can attached] to almost anything.

items.from: A team in Austria designed the device in 2013.

steps.cue: Rewrite it in the PASSIVE, keeping BY
steps.a: The device was designed by a team in Austria in 2013

steps.cue: Now leave the agent out, because it adds nothing
steps.why: Most passive sentences need no agent. Include by only when it carries information.

items.from: They are developing the system now.

steps.a: The system is being developed now

steps.cue: Now say it is finished, with the PRESENT PERFECT passive

items.from: You can attach it to almost anything.

steps.a: It can be attached to almost anything

steps.cue: Now make it a past possibility, with MAY HAVE BEEN
steps.a: It may have been attached to something else

items.from: A beetle gave him the idea.

steps.cue: Rewrite it in the PASSIVE, starting with the idea
steps.a: The idea was given to him by a beetle

steps.cue: Now start with the person instead
steps.a: He was given the idea by a beetle
steps.why: A verb with two objects allows two passives. Both are correct.

write.q: Describe how something works, in about 180 words: a machine, a process at your workplace, or something you use every day. Use the passive at least six times and in at least four different tenses. Use by only where the agent genuinely matters — and check every one before you finish.
plan: what it is and what it is for
how it is made or set up
what is happening to it now
what will be done with it
write.model:
The heating in our block is run from one boiler house that was built in 1974 and has not been substantially changed since.

Water is heated centrally and pumped through pipes that were laid under the courtyard before any of the current residents moved in. Each flat is fed from a single riser, which is why nothing can be adjusted individually: if the temperature is changed for one flat, it is changed for eleven.

The system is being surveyed at the moment, and about half the pipework has already been condemned. We were told in March that the work would be done over the summer. It has not been started.

What will actually happen, I suspect, is that two sections will be replaced, the survey will be filed, and the same conversation will be had next October.

The design is not stupid. It was built for a city where nobody paid by the unit, and it has simply never been updated for one where everybody does.
